$comment: Which test suites belong to which CI job, and which ones are ALLOWED to be
empty right now. Consumed by build/ci/Invoke-UnitTests.ps1.
Why this file exists: `dotnet test` exits 0 on an assembly containing zero
tests. Verified on this repo 2026-08-11 — an empty suite produces a TRX with
Counters total="0" and a green exit code. Without the declarations below,
the `test` job would be a green tick that has executed nothing, which is
exactly the vacuous pass 14 §13 is trying to prevent.
The rules Invoke-UnitTests.ps1 enforces:
1. Every test project under tests/ is discovered automatically. A new suite
(e.g. SlayIdleRepeat.Client.Tests) joins the `unit` group with no edit
here, and is REQUIRED to contain tests from day one.
2. A suite listed in knownEmpty may report zero tests.
3. A suite listed in knownEmpty that DOES report tests fails the build with
'stale exemption'. The entry cannot outlive the milestone that fills the
suite — removing it is forced, not remembered.
4. A name in a group's include/exclude that matches no discovered suite
fails the build. Neither list errors on its own: a typo in `include`
quietly shrinks the group and a typo in `exclude` quietly stops
excluding, and in both cases the job stays green while running a
different set of tests than this file claims it runs.
5. A knownEmpty entry naming a project that is not among the discovered
suites fails the build — a renamed or deleted project must take its
exemption with it, or the exemption sits here pre-armed for whatever
lands on that name next.
6. A knownEmpty entry must carry a well-formed `turnsOn` milestone and a
non-empty `reason`. An exemption with no milestone has no expiry.
See $knownGapInThisMechanism at the foot of this file for what these
rules deliberately do NOT catch.

unit.description: Domain, application and contract suites. Everything that needs no container — which, since the integration tier was removed, is every suite except architecture.

architecture.description: 23 §6 / 30 §9 dependency, port-purity and adapter-isolation rules. Its own job so a flake elsewhere can never mask it — 23 §6 says it fails the build.

$noIntegrationTier: 🔒 THIS REPOSITORY HAS NO INTEGRATION OR END-TO-END TEST TIER, BY DECISION.
SlayIdleRepeat.Integration.Tests was deleted and its `integration` group
removed from this file. Do not re-add either. A test that needs docker
compose, a live Postgres/Redis/MinIO, a real ASP.NET host or the Godot
runtime does not belong in this repository at all — it is not to be
relocated to a new suite, and no group here is to be pointed at one.
What replaced its three assertions: the compose-boot job in
.github/workflows/ci.yml now probes /health, the MinIO liveness endpoint and
the Prometheus scrape targets directly with build/ci/ scripts. That job boots
the stack to prove 14 §1.1's portability claim; it is CI infrastructure, not a
test tier, and nothing in it is a suite anyone writes tests into.
Every tier that remains is fast and dependency-free: Core.Tests,

note: Its stated reason was 'there are no ports with two implementations yet'.
That stopped being true on this branch: M0-09 landed IContentSourcePort
with a shared contract suite (IContentSourcePortContractTests) and two
derived fixtures, one per implementation. 24 passing cases. Rule 3 above
would have failed the build on the next run — which is the mechanism
working, and this entry moving here is what it was for.
Recorded because it was wrong in a second way nobody would have caught:
turnsOn said M1-09, and M1-09 is the BEGIN_SESSION handler. The port
catalogue and the shared contract suites are M5-01. A knownEmpty entry
can therefore be stale on its MILESTONE as well as on its test count, and
only the count is mechanically checkable — see the note at the foot of
this file.
⚠️ THE PROJECT THIS ENTRY DESCRIBES NO LONGER EXISTS. Kept as the record of
why the compose-boot job's assertions are now pwsh probes rather than a test
suite. Its three cases (API /health, object store liveness, telemetry
targets up) were carried over into ci.yml verbatim in intent, so the
vacuous-pass problem described below did not come back with the deletion.
The rest of this note is history, from when the suite was still here.
This exemption was removed rather than re-pointed at a later milestone.
Its stated reason was 'needs the compose stack, which does not exist until
M0-03'. M0-03 landed docker-compose.yml, so the reason expired — and rule 3
above (a knownEmpty entry that outlives its milestone fails as a stale
exemption) means the honest options were: fill the suite, or write a new
exemption with a new reason. Moving the milestone marker to M5 and leaving
the suite empty would have been the third option, and it is the one that
quietly turns the compose-boot job's 'run integration suite against the
live stack' step into a green tick over zero assertions for five
milestones.
So M0-03 put its own acceptance criteria in the suite instead — the API
answers /health, the object store is reachable, every telemetry scrape
target is up. See tests/SlayIdleRepeat.Integration.Tests/
ComposeStackSmokeTests.cs. The full end-to-end run of 14 §13 arrives with
the adapters (M5-05 onward) and is added alongside these, not instead.
This block is documentation. Invoke-UnitTests.ps1 reads `knownEmpty` only.

$knownGapInThisMechanism: WHAT IS NOT CHECKED, so that nobody assumes it is.
Rules 3-6 catch an exemption that is stale in its SHAPE: the suite gained
tests, the project no longer exists, the milestone marker is missing or
malformed, the reason field is blank. All of those are decidable from the
What is NOT decidable, and is therefore unenforced, is an exemption whose
REASON has stopped being true while the suite is still empty. The
Contract.Tests entry above was exactly that for the interval between
IContentSourcePort landing and the suite being populated: its reason said
'there are no ports with two implementations yet' after that had become
false. Nothing goes red for that state, because 'is this English sentence
still true' is not a predicate a script can evaluate. It was caught by a
human reading the file during the M0 review.
The mitigations that ARE in place are all indirect: the entry must name a
milestone (so it has an expiry a reader can check), it must carry a written
reason (so there is something to falsify), and the moment the suite gains a
single test the build fails. Treat a knownEmpty entry as something to
re-read at every milestone kickoff, not as something CI is watching for you.
